capabilities.tool_ref: built-in chat reply channel (not declared in tools.json)
capabilities.target: The same authenticated employee's chat session that issued the question

inputs.source: Employee question submitted via SSO-authenticated chat session
Published HR policy documents in a read-only search index; writes require two-person HR content team review

instructions.note: 'Do not give legal advice' is enforced only by instruction text; nothing structural blocks legal-sounding output. Severity is low because any resulting reply can only reach the same authenticated employee who asked, and the agent has no egress or persistence capability, so the blast radius is a single reply.

controls.name: Least-privilege, read-only credential scoped to the published policy index
controls.decay_rationale: Enforced by credential/IAM scoping outside the model; a more capable model cannot read or write anything the credential does not permit.

controls.name: Network-layer egress denial beyond the policy index and chat channel, pen-test verified
controls.decay_rationale: Enforced at the network layer, independent of model behavior, and confirmed empirically by a penetration test rather than only declared. No destination exists for exfiltrated data beyond the two declared channels.

controls.name: Chat client does not render images or auto-fetch links
controls.decay_rationale: Covert-channel exfiltration via rendered links or images is not possible regardless of model capability, since the client never fetches external content.

controls.name: Two-person review required to publish content into the policy index
controls.decay_rationale: Enforced by the HR content publishing process, not by the model; reduces the likelihood that a single compromised or malicious author injects instructions into policy text.

controls.name: Model version pinned; any upgrade requires a change ticket
controls.decay_rationale: The model cannot change silently; upgrades go through a reviewed change process, so the model_upgrade trigger cannot fire without a corresponding reassessment opportunity.

controls.name: Replies are bound to the requester's own authenticated chat session; no alternate recipient is addressable
controls.decay_rationale: The destination is fixed by the system of record (the session that authenticated the requester), not chosen by the model, so it cannot be redirected regardless of model behavior.

controls.name: Tool manifest declares exactly one tool (policy_search.search); no other actions are available
controls.decay_rationale: This is effectively an allowlist of one tool. It holds today, but per control_decay.md it fails open the moment a new tool or MCP server is added, since new tools are permitted by default.

findings.title: Lethal-trifecta (TC1) preconditions exist via policy-document content, but the path is currently severed by the absence of any egress-capable tool

attack_path.note: HR content team authored text, gated by two-person review before publish
Agent retrieves and quotes document text into its context
Agent returns the quoted text, and any injected instructions within it, to the requesting employee only

forecast.watch_signal: tools.json gains an entry beyond policy_search.search (especially anything with an external destination or a model-chosen recipient), or the policy_search credential scope widens to a data store containing confidential or restricted HR data (e.g., case files, compensation records).

evidence.observation: The agent is instructed to quote the policy verbatim, so any text present in the index, including injected instructions, would be reproduced to the user.
Exactly one tool is declared, policy_search.search, with no egress-capable action and no parameter for choosing a recipient.

Write access to the policy index is restricted to the HR content team with two-person review; the agent's credential is read-only and scoped to that index; the agent has no other tools, no memory, and no network egress, verified by a pen test.

Replies are delivered only within the same authenticated chat session that issued the question, so despite being a send-type action, no data crosses the trust boundary to a different or attacker-controlled destination; is_egress is scored false on this basis.

recommendations.action: Add provenance or integrity tagging to policy index entries (e.g., a content hash recorded at publish time and checked at retrieval) so any out-of-band modification of published text is detectable before it reaches the model.
Log policy_search queries together with the returned document ids so a reassessment triggered by data_scope_expansion or new_tool can trace which content reached which reply.

Treat any addition to tools.json, any MCP server connection, or any widening of the policy_search credential scope as a significant change requiring a PARA reassessment before deployment, since these are exactly the controls that currently sever the lethal trifecta.
Declare explicit max_unattended_steps and max_runtime_minutes for this single-turn search-then-reply flow so autonomy bounds are verifiable rather than implicit.

rating.rationale: The only present-day path (published policy content read via policy_search and returned via chat_reply) scores low on the rubric: the source is internal (gated by two-person review) or trusted (the authenticated requester), and the sink is S1 limited, because is_egress is false on chat_reply (replies are bound to the requester's own authenticated session, not a model-chosen or external destination) and no further egress is reachable (network egress is denied and pen-test verified, and only one non-egress tool is declared). Residual stays at the rubric floor of low; the structural controls (scoped read-only credential, network egress denial, session-bound reply, non-rendering client, two-person review, model pinning) are independent of model capability and do not need behavioral credit. The forecast rises to high because two of those controls are only partially_dependent or scope-bound: the single-tool manifest is an allowlist that fails open under new_tool/new_mcp_server, and the scoped credential's protection is only as good as its current scope under data_scope_expansion. If either trigger fires, together they reopen the classic lethal-trifecta shape (untrusted-adjacent or internal content read plus an egress-capable action over confidential-or-higher data), projected at high. Model pinning with a change-ticket gate means model_upgrade is a governed rather than silent trigger, which is why it is listed but does not by itself dominate the forecast.

limitations: This assessment reflects declared design and configuration artifacts (system prompt, tool manifest, runtime notes) as of the review date; it does not reflect observed runtime behavior of the deployed agent.

No MCP configuration, IaC, or source code was provided. The tool manifest (tools.json) is the only capability enumeration available, so the claim that no other tool exists cannot be independently verified beyond what is declared; confidence on the single-tool containment claim is medium rather than high for this reason.

Autonomy step and runtime limits (max_unattended_steps, max_runtime_minutes) are not declared anywhere in the provided artifacts and are recorded as null rather than inferred; this is a documentation gap worth closing even though the design is structurally a single search-then-reply turn.
